abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev Value (m : ℕ) := Fin m → ℝ
def dot {m : ℕ} (v w : Value m) : ℝ := ∑ k, v k * w k
def normSq {m : ℕ} (v : Value m) : ℝ := dot v v
noncomputable def velocity {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => deriv (fun r => u (x, r) k) t
noncomputable def acceleration {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => deriv (fun r => velocity u x r k) t
noncomputable def spatial {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => u (y, t) k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def spatialSecond {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial u j y t k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def laplacian {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m := ∑ j, spatialSecond u j x t
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  normSq (velocity u x t) + ∑ j, normSq (spatial u j x t)
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, density u x t
def Smooth {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u {p | 0 < p.2}
def UnitValued {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t → normSq (u (x, t)) = 1
def Normal {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, acceleration u x t - laplacian u x t = a • u (x, t)

item.text: The basis proof replaces the original dominated-convergence and box-integration arguments with native differentiation-under-the-integral and whole-space integration-by-parts theorems. I’ll preserve those replacements and prove all six class-3 results internally. The target still requires integrability and differentiability, with no assumption on the regularity of the normality scalar.

{"path": "nl0/references/logical-rules.md", "total_lines": 78, "start": 1, "end": 78, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 75, "requested_end": 200, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning."}

spec.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.

and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
spec.conclusion: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

hypotheses.statement: u is jointly C∞ on ℝⁿ×(0,∞).
q∈ℝᵐ satisfies |q|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_x u(x,t)=a u(x,t), with Δ_x u=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise. No regularity or global choice of the scalar is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊆ℝⁿ such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.definition: Space = Fin n → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝⁿ, with its product norm, Borel structure and topology.
Value = Fin m → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝᵐ, with its product norm and topology.
For v,w∈Value, dot(v,w)=∑_{k∈Fin m} v(k)w(k). This is the Euclidean dot product.
For v∈Value, normSq(v)=dot(v,v), the Euclidean norm squared.
In the fixed standard coordinates, ubar(x,t)=u(x,t) for t>0 and ubar(x,t)=q for t≤0. This is a total representative only; its definition asserts no regularity at t=0.

definitions.type: open-domain notation: subset of Space × ℝ
definitions.definition: U={(x,t)∈Space×ℝ:0<t}. All calculus assertions about ubar are restricted to U.
For j∈Fin n, basis(j)=Pi.single j 1 is the standard vector with coordinate 1 at j and 0 elsewhere.

definitions.type: notation for calculus, topology and measure
definitions.definition: For maps between the stated normed spaces, Df and fderiv ℝ f denote the real Fréchet derivative (the total library operator, set to zero when no derivative exists); deriv f is the analogous one-variable real derivative. HasDerivAt f a t means f is differentiable at t with derivative a. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt mean C^r regularity on a set and at a point, with ∞ meaning all finite orders and ω analytic. minSmoothness(κ,2) is 2 for real/complex normed fields and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt κ f p means D(Df)(p)(v)(w)=D(Df)(p)(w)(v) for all directions v,w. 𝓝 t is the neighborhood filter. support f={x:f(x)≠0}, tsupport f is its closure, and HasCompactSupport f means tsupport f is compact. ContinuousOn has its usual relative-set meaning. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function; Integrable means this measurability and finite integral of the norm, and IntegrableOn f C μ means Integrable f (μ restricted to C). The Bochner integral ∫ f dμ uses the library total convention; it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral when f is real and integrable. A set indicator equals its function on the set and zero off it. ae means outside a μ-null set. ‖c‖ₑ denotes the extended nonnegative norm used for ESeminormedAddMonoid; ordinary real numbers have finite extended norm. The standard structure names in source contracts carry their usual mathematical meanings (in particular OpensMeasurableSpace: open sets measurable; BorelSpace: measurable structure is Borel; IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts: compact sets have finite measure; IsAddHaarMeasure: additive Haar measure).
V(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) t, for each x,t and k∈Fin m.
A(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦V(x,r)_k) t.
Psp(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
Ssp(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
L(x,t)=∑_{j∈Fin n} Ssp(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.

dx is canonical Lebesgue volume on Space: the product of the usual real Lebesgue measures in its fixed standard coordinates. It is the original dx on ℝⁿ. Spatial integrals without a displayed measure use dx.
e(x,t)=normSq(V(x,t))+∑_{j∈Fin n} normSq(Psp(j,x,t)). This is |u_t|²+∑_j |∂_{x_j}u|² at positive times, with the Euclidean/Frobenius squares and coefficient 1 on each term.
E(t)=∫_{Space} e(x,t) dx, using the total integral convention until integrability is proved. At positive times when integrable this is the original finite energy integral.
W(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_{j∈Fin n} dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)).

propositions.statement: For any measurable topological space Z whose open sets are measurable, any normed additive commutative group Y0, any measure μ on Z finite on compact sets, and any f:Z→Y0, if f is continuous and has compact topological support, then f is μ-integrable.

hypotheses: Z is a measurable topological space with OpensMeasurableSpace, Y0 is a normed additive commutative group, and μ is a measure finite on compact sets.
The topological support of f is compact.

propositions.statement: Let α be a measurable space, μ a measure on α, κ an RCLike field, and Y0 a normed additive commutative group with both real and κ normed-space structures. The fixed standard-coordinate representation Space=Fin n→ℝ and Value=Fin m→ℝ identifies the original Euclidean map with ubar restricted to U; Euclidean squares are normSq and the original dx is the product Lebesgue volume dx with no scaling. At positive times V=u_t, A=u_tt, Psp(j)=∂_j u, Ssp(j)=∂_jj u, L=Δ_xu, e=|u_t|²+∑_j|∂_j u|² and E is the same total integral expression, finite whenever e is integrable. The fields ubar,V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d are C∞ on U for every j∈Fin n. For every x∈Space, t>0, k∈Fin m and j∈Fin n: HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) V(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦V(x,r)_k) A(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j,x,r)_k) W(j,x,t)_k t; fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Psp(j,x,t)_k; fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=W(j,x,t)_k; and fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Ssp(j,x,t)_k. In particular the time derivative of Psp(j) and the spatial j derivative of V coincide. Moreover HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t, with d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_j dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)). argument.text: H001 fixes positive finite dimensions. Use the fixed standard coordinates on both original Euclidean spaces. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. At a point of U a neighborhood stays in U, so all derivatives there are local and independent of the extension at nonpositive times. H002 therefore gives C∞ regularity of ubar on U. The derivative definitions, finite coordinate sums and the measure identification give the asserted meanings of V,A,Psp,Ssp,L,e,E once their actual derivative identities are checked below. Record F001: this coordinate representation, measure and norm identification is faithful, and ubar is C∞ on U.

produces.statement: The coordinate identities are continuous linear isomorphisms preserving the original Euclidean differential calculus; normSq is the Euclidean square and dx is the original Lebesgue measure. ubar restricted to U is u and ubar is C∞ on U. All derivatives at positive times are independent of the arbitrary extension.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x,t>0,j,k as declared and put p=(x,t), w(y,r)=ubar(y,r)_k, T=(0,1), Xdir=(basis(j),0). F001 and continuous linear scalar projection give w C∞ on the open set U. Apply M006 over ℝ, with domain Space×ℝ, scalar codomain and both smoothness orders ∞: ∞+1=∞ supplies the order inequality, so Dw is C∞ on U. The derivative of the affine time injection r↦(x,r) sends h to (0,h); the derivative of y↦(y,t) sends h to (h,0). The ordinary chain rule identifies V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir, first as HasDerivAt or HasFDerivAt assertions, then as equalities by uniqueness. These identities hold on all U, not just at p. Evaluation at a fixed direction is continuous linear, so the identities and smoothness of Dw show that V and every Psp(j) are C∞ on U, componentwise and hence as finite vector-valued maps. In particular the actual time derivative of each coordinate of ubar is V. Record F002 with these first-derivative and smoothness facts.

produces.statement: V and Psp(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For every x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m, HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x0,r)_k0) V(x0,t1)_k0 t1; the spatial derivative in direction basis(j0) is Psp(j0,x0,t1)_k0. At the chosen p, V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir.

argument.text: Put Hess(v,w0)=D(Dw)(p)(v)(w0). Apply M006 again, this time to the C∞ map Dw with its continuous-linear-map codomain, and iterate for higher derivatives as needed; U is open and the ∞ order inequality remains valid. Differentiate the fixed evaluations from S002 by the chain rule. This gives ∂_t Psp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(T,Xdir), ∂_j V(x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,T), A(x,t)_k=Hess(T,T), and Ssp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,Xdir). F001 gives C² regularity of w at p because p∈U. Apply M005 over ℝ at order 2, where minSmoothness(ℝ,2)=2, to get Hess(T,Xdir)=Hess(Xdir,T). By the definition of W the common value is W(j,x,t)_k. The same derivative closure and fixed evaluations show A,Ssp(j),W(j) C∞ on U; this holds at every positive point and for every coordinate. Record F003: the full second-derivative regularity and the actual time derivative identities for V and Psp.

produces.statement: A, Ssp(j0), W(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For all x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m,j0∈Fin n, HasDerivAt (r↦V(x0,r)_k0) A(x0,t1)_k0 t1 and HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j0,x0,r)_k0) W(j0,x0,t1)_k0 t1. The spatial j0 derivative of V_k0 is W(j0)_k0 and the spatial j0 derivative of Psp(j0)_k0 is Ssp(j0)_k0.

argument.text: Apply M004 over ℝ to the time function V(x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using F003, to obtain derivative 2 V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k for its square. Apply M004 also to Psp(j,x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using its time derivative W(j,x,t)_k from F003, to obtain 2 Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k. The coordinate k and spatial index j are arbitrary; finite-sum differentiation therefore gives HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) [2∑_k V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k+2∑_j∑_k Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k] t. Finite distributivity identifies the bracket with d(x,t). Smooth finite products and sums of F002 and F003 also show e and d are C∞ on U. Record F004: the displayed HasDerivAt identity with derivative d, and C∞ regularity of e,d.

argument.text: The spatial derivative identities for ubar, Psp and V are their definitions; F002 and F003 verify that they are genuine derivatives at positive times. Combining F001–F004 proves all regularity, mixed-derivative and energy-derivative clauses. Since x,t,j,k were arbitrary, close their quantifiers. The identified Laplacian is exactly L=∑_j Ssp(j), and the identified density and measure give the original total energy expression E without any change of coefficient. This proves N001.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. The inequalities 0<t0/2<3t0/2 allow H006 to choose compact C such that u=q off C throughout J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2). All times of J are positive, so the definition of ubar gives the same equality for ubar. In particular t0∈I. Record F001: C is compact and ubar=q on Cᶜ×J.

argument.text: A compact subset C of the Hausdorff finite-dimensional space is closed. Thus O=Cᶜ×I is open. At each arbitrary p∈O the equality in F001 holds on a whole neighborhood: ubar is locally the constant q. Apply M007 to ubar and that constant on this neighborhood. The constant has zero derivative (its increments are zero), so D ubar(p)=0. This holds at every point of O. Reapply M007 to this derivative map and the zero map at every point of O; its derivative is again zero. Induction on the positive order now gives all iterated positive-order Fréchet derivatives zero on O: the first-order case is established; if the order-ℓ derivative map is zero throughout O, each point has a neighborhood on which that map is the constant zero, so M007 makes its next derivative zero there. The same chain-rule directional evaluations as in N001 identify V,A,Psp,Ssp,W with evaluations of the first two derivatives. Consequently V=A=Psp(j)=Ssp(j)=W(j)=0 on O for all j, and the formulas for e,d make both zero there. Record F002 with this universal vanishing conclusion.

produces.statement: Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on O=Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j1),Ssp(j1),W(j1),e,d vanish there for every j1∈Fin n.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r∈I and take the family of sections specified in the local declaration. By N001 each component section is continuous on the whole spatial space; e,d are continuous as well. Finite products, sums and dot products preserve continuity. F002 makes each of these sections zero off C. For an arbitrary section h in this family, support h⊆C. Since C is closed, its closure tsupport h is also contained in C; tsupport h is closed and hence a compact closed subset of the compact C. Apply M001 with domain Space, codomain ℝ and measure dx to h. This is a Borel real normed coordinate space; its Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. For example a compact set is contained in some finite coordinate box, whose product Lebesgue measure is finite, and monotonicity bounds the compact set's measure. Therefore the source gives dx-integrability of every such h. Record F003: all the stated sections at r have compact topological support contained in C and are integrable.

produces.statement: At the arbitrary r∈I, every h in family is continuous with tsupport h⊆C, has compact topological support, and is dx-integrable.

argument.text: The conclusions hold for every r∈I and every stated component, product, dot product and finite linear combination. Since t0∈I, this proves integrability of e(·,t0). In particular every positive time has an integrable energy density. No vanishing assertion at the endpoints of J has been used.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and choose C from N002 with its full conclusions. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2), eta=t0/4>0, Ktime=[t0−eta,t0+eta], stime=(t0−eta,t0+eta). Explicitly t0−eta=3t0/4>t0/2 and t0+eta=5t0/4<3t0/2. Thus Ktime⊂I⊂(0,∞), and stime is an open neighborhood of t0. N002 supplies vanishing of d off C for all these times, and integrability and continuity of the spatial sections e,d throughout I.

Set Kprod=C×Ktime. Compactness of C from N002 and compactness of the closed bounded real interval Ktime show that Kprod is compact. It lies in U. N001 makes d continuous on U, so its restriction is continuous on Kprod. Apply M008 to d on Kprod to obtain a real bound for |d|. Record F001: there exists a real bound on Kprod. This existence assertion is valid also for empty C.

argument.text: Choose B0 from F001 and put B=max(B0,0), bnd=B·1_C. The compact subset C of the Hausdorff coordinate space is closed and hence Borel measurable. Its Lebesgue measure is finite: compactness bounds it in a finite coordinate box and dx of that box is the finite product of its side lengths. The real number B has finite extended norm. M009, with scalar value B and set C, gives IntegrableOn (constant B) C dx. M010, using measurability of C, turns this into Integrable bnd dx. Thus record F002: bnd is an integrable nonnegative bound, and |d(x,r)|≤B on C×Ktime.

argument.text: For each spatial x and every r∈stime, if x∈C the compact bound in F002 gives |d(x,r)|≤B=bnd(x); if x∉C, N002 gives d(x,r)=0 and bnd(x)=0. Consequently the entire predicate ∀ r∈stime, |d(x,r)|≤bnd(x) holds for every x, and hence for dx-almost every x with a single, empty exceptional set. Separately N001 gives HasDerivAt (s↦e(x,s)) d(x,r) r for every x and every r∈stime, because all these times are positive. Thus this universal-in-r predicate also holds for dx-almost every x. N001 gives continuity of e(·,r) for r∈stime and of d(·,t0); continuous real functions on the Borel coordinate space are strongly measurable and hence ae strongly measurable. This supplies eventual measurability of e because stime is a neighborhood. N002 gives integrability of e(·,t0). Record F003 with these premises, preserving the ae-first order in both quantified hypotheses.

spec.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
spec.conclusion: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

argument.text: H001 fixes positive finite dimensions. Use the fixed standard coordinates on both original Euclidean spaces. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. At a point of U a neighborhood stays in U, so all derivatives there are local and independent of the extension at nonpositive times. H002 therefore gives C∞ regularity of ubar on U. The derivative definitions, finite coordinate sums and the measure identification give the asserted meanings of V,A,Psp,Ssp,L,e,E once their actual derivative identities are checked below. Record F001: this coordinate representation, measure and norm identification is faithful, and ubar is C∞ on U.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x,t>0,j,k as declared and put p=(x,t), w(y,r)=ubar(y,r)_k, T=(0,1), Xdir=(basis(j),0). F001 and continuous linear scalar projection give w C∞ on the open set U. Apply M006 over ℝ, with domain Space×ℝ, scalar codomain and both smoothness orders ∞: ∞+1=∞ supplies the order inequality, so Dw is C∞ on U. The derivative of the affine time injection r↦(x,r) sends h to (0,h); the derivative of y↦(y,t) sends h to (h,0). The ordinary chain rule identifies V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir, first as HasDerivAt or HasFDerivAt assertions, then as equalities by uniqueness. These identities hold on all U, not just at p. Evaluation at a fixed direction is continuous linear, so the identities and smoothness of Dw show that V and every Psp(j) are C∞ on U, componentwise and hence as finite vector-valued maps. In particular the actual time derivative of each coordinate of ubar is V. Record F002 with these first-derivative and smoothness facts.

produces.statement: V and Psp(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For every x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m, HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x0,r)_k0) V(x0,t1)_k0 t1; the spatial derivative in direction basis(j0) is Psp(j0,x0,t1)_k0. At the chosen p, V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir.

argument.text: Put Hess(v,w0)=D(Dw)(p)(v)(w0). Apply M006 again, this time to the C∞ map Dw with its continuous-linear-map codomain, and iterate for higher derivatives as needed; U is open and the ∞ order inequality remains valid. Differentiate the fixed evaluations from S002 by the chain rule. This gives ∂_t Psp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(T,Xdir), ∂_j V(x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,T), A(x,t)_k=Hess(T,T), and Ssp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,Xdir). F001 gives C² regularity of w at p because p∈U. Apply M005 over ℝ at order 2, where minSmoothness(ℝ,2)=2, to get Hess(T,Xdir)=Hess(Xdir,T). By the definition of W the common value is W(j,x,t)_k. The same derivative closure and fixed evaluations show A,Ssp(j),W(j) C∞ on U; this holds at every positive point and for every coordinate. Record F003: the full second-derivative regularity and the actual time derivative identities for V and Psp.

produces.statement: A, Ssp(j0), W(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For all x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m,j0∈Fin n, HasDerivAt (r↦V(x0,r)_k0) A(x0,t1)_k0 t1 and HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j0,x0,r)_k0) W(j0,x0,t1)_k0 t1. argument.text: Apply M004 over ℝ to the time function V(x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using F003, to obtain derivative 2 V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k for its square. Apply M004 also to Psp(j,x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using its time derivative W(j,x,t)_k from F003, to obtain 2 Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k. The coordinate k and spatial index j are arbitrary; finite-sum differentiation therefore gives HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) [2∑_k V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k+2∑_j∑_k Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k] t. Finite distributivity identifies the bracket with d(x,t). Smooth finite products and sums of F002 and F003 also show e and d are C∞ on U. Record F004: the displayed HasDerivAt identity with derivative d, and C∞ regularity of e,d.

produces.statement: e and d are C∞ on U, and for the arbitrary x and t>0, HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t.

argument.text: The spatial derivative identities for ubar, Psp and V are their definitions; F002 and F003 verify that they are genuine derivatives at positive times. Combining F001–F004 proves all regularity, mixed-derivative and energy-derivative clauses. Since x,t,j,k were arbitrary, close their quantifiers. The identified Laplacian is exactly L=∑_j Ssp(j), and the identified density and measure give the original total energy expression E without any change of coefficient. This proves N001.

The family consists of all scalar component sections of V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j), and e,d, the five listed products in N002, and their finite sums, dot products and real linear combinations, at time r.
Take arbitrary h in this family.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. The inequalities 0<t0/2<3t0/2 allow H006 to choose compact C such that u=q off C throughout J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2). All times of J are positive, so the definition of ubar gives the same equality for ubar. In particular t0∈I. Record F001: C is compact and ubar=q on Cᶜ×J.

argument.text: A compact subset C of the Hausdorff finite-dimensional space is closed. Thus O=Cᶜ×I is open. At each arbitrary p∈O the equality in F001 holds on a whole neighborhood: ubar is locally the constant q. Apply M007 to ubar and that constant on this neighborhood. The constant has zero derivative (its increments are zero), so D ubar(p)=0. This holds at every point of O. Reapply M007 to this derivative map and the zero map at every point of O; its derivative is again zero. Induction on the positive order now gives all iterated positive-order Fréchet derivatives zero on O: the first-order case is established; if the order-ℓ derivative map is zero throughout O, each point has a neighborhood on which that map is the constant zero, so M007 makes its next derivative zero there. The same chain-rule directional evaluations as in N001 identify V,A,Psp,Ssp,W with evaluations of the first two derivatives. Consequently V=A=Psp(j)=Ssp(j)=W(j)=0 on O for all j, and the formulas for e,d make both zero there. Record F002 with this universal vanishing conclusion.

produces.statement: Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on O=Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j1),Ssp(j1),W(j1),e,d vanish there for every j1∈Fin n.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r∈I and take the family of sections specified in the local declaration. By N001 each component section is continuous on the whole spatial space; e,d are continuous as well. Finite products, sums and dot products preserve continuity. F002 makes each of these sections zero off C. For an arbitrary section h in this family, support h⊆C. Since C is closed, its closure tsupport h is also contained in C; tsupport h is closed and hence a compact closed subset of the compact C. Apply M001 with domain Space, codomain ℝ and measure dx to h. This is a Borel real normed coordinate space; its Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. For example a compact set is contained in some finite coordinate box, whose product Lebesgue measure is finite, and monotonicity bounds the compact set's measure. Therefore the source gives dx-integrability of every such h. Record F003: all the stated sections at r have compact topological support contained in C and are integrable.

produces.statement: At the arbitrary r∈I, every h in family is continuous with tsupport h⊆C, has compact topological support, and is dx-integrable.

argument.text: The conclusions hold for every r∈I and every stated component, product, dot product and finite linear combination. Since t0∈I, this proves integrability of e(·,t0). The existence and vanishing conclusions depend only on the chosen slab and thus give the full existential statement N002 after closing the choice of C and the arbitrary t0. In particular every positive time has an integrable energy density. No vanishing assertion at the endpoints of J has been used.

Choose B0 with |d(x,r)|≤B0 on Kprod from F001.
Put bnd(x)=B if x∈C, and bnd(x)=0 otherwise.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and choose C from N002 with its full conclusions. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2), eta=t0/4>0, Ktime=[t0−eta,t0+eta], stime=(t0−eta,t0+eta). Explicitly t0−eta=3t0/4>t0/2 and t0+eta=5t0/4<3t0/2. Thus Ktime⊂I⊂(0,∞), and stime is an open neighborhood of t0. N002 supplies vanishing of d off C for all these times, and integrability and continuity of the spatial sections e,d throughout I.

Set Kprod=C×Ktime. Compactness of C from N002 and compactness of the closed bounded real interval Ktime show that Kprod is compact. It lies in U. N001 makes d continuous on U, so its restriction is continuous on Kprod. Apply M008 to d on Kprod to obtain a real bound for |d|. Record F001: there exists a real bound on Kprod. This existence assertion is valid also for empty C.

produces.statement: There exists a real c0 such that |d(x1,r1)|≤c0 for every (x1,r1)∈Kprod.

argument.text: Choose B0 from F001 and put B=max(B0,0), bnd=B·1_C. The compact subset C of the Hausdorff coordinate space is closed and hence Borel measurable. Its Lebesgue measure is finite: compactness bounds it in a finite coordinate box and dx of that box is the finite product of its side lengths. The real number B has finite extended norm. M009, with scalar value B and set C, gives IntegrableOn (constant B) C dx. M010, using measurability of C, turns this into Integrable bnd dx. Thus record F002: bnd is an integrable nonnegative bound, and |d(x,r)|≤B on C×Ktime.

produces.statement: bnd is dx-integrable, B≥0, and |d(x1,r1)|≤B whenever (x1,r1)∈C×Ktime; bnd=B on C and zero off C.

argument.text: For each spatial x and every r∈stime, if x∈C the compact bound in F002 gives |d(x,r)|≤B=bnd(x); if x∉C, N002 gives d(x,r)=0 and bnd(x)=0. Consequently the entire predicate ∀ r∈stime, |d(x,r)|≤bnd(x) holds for every x, and hence for dx-almost every x with a single, empty exceptional set. Separately N001 gives HasDerivAt (s↦e(x,s)) d(x,r) r for every x and every r∈stime, because all these times are positive. Thus this universal-in-r predicate also holds for dx-almost every x. N001 gives continuity of e(·,r) for r∈stime and of d(·,t0); continuous real functions on the Borel coordinate space are strongly measurable and hence ae strongly measurable. This supplies eventual measurability of e because stime is a neighborhood. N002 gives integrability of e(·,t0). Record F003 with these premises, preserving the ae-first order in both quantified hypotheses.

produces.statement: stime∈𝓝 t0. Eventually r→t0, e(·,r) is dx-ae strongly measurable; e(·,t0) is dx-integrable; d(·,t0) is dx-ae strongly measurable. For dx-almost every x1, for every r1∈stime, |d(x1,r1)|≤bnd(x1). For dx-almost every x1, for every r1∈stime, HasDerivAt (s↦e(x1,s)) d(x1,r1) r1. Each of the two ae assertions follows from its corresponding everywhere-in-space assertion.

argument.text: Apply M002 with α=Space, μ=dx, real parameter and codomain, F(r,x)=e(x,r), F'(r,x)=d(x,r), basepoint t0, neighborhood stime and bound bnd. F003 gives its neighborhood, eventual measurability, base integrability, derivative-section measurability, ae-first bound and ae-first derivative premises. F002 gives integrability of the bound. M002 concludes Integrable d(·,t0) and HasDerivAt (r↦∫ e(x,r) dx) (∫ d(x,t0) dx) t0. By the definition of E this is the desired derivative statement for the actual energy integral. N002 ensures that the integrals e defining E are finite at all positive times, so this is differentiability of the requested finite function.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x and t>0. H004 and the coordinate identification in N001 give ∑_k ubar(x,r)_k²=1 for every r>0, hence on a neighborhood of t. For arbitrary k apply M004 over ℝ to ubar(x,·)_k multiplied by itself; N001 supplies its actual derivative V(x,t)_k. The square has derivative 2 ubar(x,t)_k V(x,t)_k. Differentiating the finite sum gives derivative 2 dot(ubar(x,t),V(x,t)). Since the sum agrees locally with the constant 1, its derivative is zero by locality and uniqueness of derivatives. Division by 2 yields dot(ubar,V)=0; commutativity of real multiplication yields dot(V,ubar)=0. Record F001: these two tangency identities at (x,t).

The actual directional derivatives from N001 are Df(x)v=W(j,x,t0)_k and Dg(x)v=Ssp(j,x,t0)_k. By N002 at time t0, all three products (Df v)g, f(Dg v) and fg are continuous with compact support and integrable: they are W(j)_k Psp(j)_k, V_k Ssp(j)_k and V_k Psp(j)_k. argument.text: Apply M003 on the finite-dimensional real space Space with its Borel structure, canonical Lebesgue additive Haar measure dx, scalar field ℝ, functions f,g and direction v. argument.text: Because k was arbitrary, F002 holds for every k∈Fin m. Sum these finitely many identities. N002 supplies integrability of each summand, so finite-sum linearity commutes integral and sum. Expanding dot gives ∫ dot(V,Ssp(j)) = −∫ dot(W(j),Psp(j)). Real multiplication commutes in each coordinate, hence dot(W(j),Psp(j))=dot(Psp(j),W(j)). Negating and rearranging gives ∫ dot(Psp(j),W(j)) = −∫ dot(V,Ssp(j)). Both integrands are integrable by N002, as are all the auxiliary products already checked. Record F003: the integration-by-parts identity at t0,j, including those integrability assertions.

produces.statement: At t0,j, ∫ dot(Psp(j,x1,t0),W(j,x1,t0)) dx1 = −∫ dot(V(x1,t0),Ssp(j,x1,t0)) dx1. Both integrands are integrable, and each of V_k1 Ssp(j)_k1, W(j)_k1 Psp(j)_k1 and V_k1 Psp(j)_k1 at this time is integrable for every k1∈Fin m.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. N002 gives integrability of e(·,t0), d(·,t0), each component product V_k A_k, Psp(j)_k W(j)_k and V_k Ssp(j)_k, and their dot products and finite linear combinations. Thus every integral in the following finite calculation is well-defined and finite. N003 gives HasDerivAt E (∫ d(x,t0) dx) t0. produces.statement: HasDerivAt E (∫ d(x1,t0) dx1) t0; e(·,t0), d(·,t0), dot(V,A), every dot(Psp(j1),W(j1)), every dot(V,Ssp(j1)), and their finite real linear combinations at t0 are dx-integrable.

argument.text:
Use F001 to distribute finite sums and real scalar factors through integrals, the definition of d, N005 for each j, and L=∑_j Ssp(j). All integrands here are evaluated at (x,t0):
∫ d = 2∫ dot(V,A) + 2∑_j ∫ dot(Psp(j),W(j))
     = 2∫ dot(V,A) − 2∑_j ∫ dot(V,Ssp(j))
     = 2∫ dot(V,A−∑_j Ssp(j))
     = 2∫ dot(V,A−L) = 0.
The penultimate algebra uses finite distributivity of dot and the integral's linearity for the integrable terms in F001. The last equality follows from the pointwise cancellation N004 at every x and positive t0, followed by the integral of the zero function. Hence the derivative value in F001 is zero. argument.text: HasDerivAt E 0 t0 in F002 implies differentiability at t0 and E'(t0)=0 by the definition and uniqueness of the derivative. N002 already gives integrability of e(·,t0), so E(t0) is the actual finite energy, not a value assigned by the total integral convention. N001 identifies every derivative, Euclidean square, Frobenius finite sum and the measure with the original target. Thus the original density has coefficient 1 on |u_t|² and on each spatial derivative square, and the original E is differentiable with derivative zero at every positive time. Close the arbitrary t0 to obtain P, including integrability. No assertion at time zero is made.

spec.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
spec.conclusion: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

hypotheses.statement: u is jointly C∞ on ℝⁿ×(0,∞).
q∈ℝᵐ satisfies |q|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_x u(x,t)=a u(x,t), with Δ_x u=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise. No regularity or global choice of the scalar is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊆ℝⁿ such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.type: notation for calculus, topology and measure
definitions.definition: For maps between the stated normed spaces, Df and fderiv ℝ f denote the real Fréchet derivative (the total library operator, set to zero when no derivative exists); deriv f is the analogous one-variable real derivative. HasDerivAt f a t means f is differentiable at t with derivative a. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt mean C^r regularity on a set and at a point, with ∞ meaning all finite orders and ω analytic. minSmoothness(κ,2) is 2 for real/complex normed fields and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt κ f p means D(Df)(p)(v)(w)=D(Df)(p)(w)(v) for all directions v,w. 𝓝 t is the neighborhood filter. support f={x:f(x)≠0}, tsupport f is its closure, and HasCompactSupport f means tsupport f is compact. ContinuousOn has its usual relative-set meaning. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function; Integrable means this measurability and finite integral of the norm, and IntegrableOn f C μ means Integrable f (μ restricted to C). The Bochner integral ∫ f dμ uses the library total convention; it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral when f is real and integrable. A set indicator equals its function on the set and zero off it. ae means outside a μ-null set. ‖c‖ₑ denotes the extended nonnegative norm used for ESeminormedAddMonoid; ordinary real numbers have finite extended norm. The standard structure names in source contracts carry their usual mathematical meanings (in particular OpensMeasurableSpace: open sets measurable; BorelSpace: measurable structure is Borel; IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts: compact sets have finite measure; IsAddHaarMeasure: additive Haar measure).
V(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) t, for each x,t and k∈Fin m.
A(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦V(x,r)_k) t.
Psp(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
Ssp(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
L(x,t)=∑_{j∈Fin n} Ssp(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.

dx is canonical Lebesgue volume on Space: the product of the usual real Lebesgue measures in its fixed standard coordinates. It is the original dx on ℝⁿ. Spatial integrals without a displayed measure use dx.
e(x,t)=normSq(V(x,t))+∑_{j∈Fin n} normSq(Psp(j,x,t)). This is |u_t|²+∑_j |∂_{x_j}u|² at positive times, with the Euclidean/Frobenius squares and coefficient 1 on each term.
E(t)=∫_{Space} e(x,t) dx, using the total integral convention until integrability is proved. At positive times when integrable this is the original finite energy integral.
W(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_{j∈Fin n} dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)).

The fixed standard-coordinate representation Space=Fin n→ℝ and Value=Fin m→ℝ identifies the original Euclidean map with ubar restricted to U; Euclidean squares are normSq and the original dx is the product Lebesgue volume dx with no scaling. At positive times V=u_t, A=u_tt, Psp(j)=∂_j u, Ssp(j)=∂_jj u, L=Δ_xu, e=|u_t|²+∑_j|∂_j u|² and E is the same total integral expression, finite whenever e is integrable. The fields ubar,V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d are C∞ on U for every j∈Fin n. For every x∈Space, t>0, k∈Fin m and j∈Fin n: HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) V(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦V(x,r)_k) A(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j,x,r)_k) W(j,x,t)_k t; fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Psp(j,x,t)_k; fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=W(j,x,t)_k; and fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Ssp(j,x,t)_k. In particular the time derivative of Psp(j) and the spatial j derivative of V coincide. Moreover HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t, with d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_j dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)). No assertion of regularity across zero is made.

Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d vanish there. For every r∈I and j∈Fin n,k∈Fin m, all scalar component spatial sections of V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j), the sections e(·,r),d(·,r), and the products V_k A_k, Psp(j)_k W(j)_k, V_k Ssp(j)_k, V_k Psp(j)_k, W(j)_k Psp(j)_k at time r are continuous, have tsupport contained in C, and are dx-integrable. Their finite sums, dot products and finite real linear combinations are likewise continuous, compactly supported in C and integrable. In particular e(·,t) is dx-integrable for every t>0.

argument.text: H001 fixes positive finite dimensions. Use the fixed standard coordinates on both original Euclidean spaces. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. At a point of U a neighborhood stays in U, so all derivatives there are local and independent of the extension at nonpositive times. H002 therefore gives C∞ regularity of ubar on U. The derivative definitions, finite coordinate sums and the measure identification give the asserted meanings of V,A,Psp,Ssp,L,e,E once their actual derivative identities are checked below. Record F001: this coordinate representation, measure and norm identification is faithful, and ubar is C∞ on U.

produces.statement: The coordinate identities are continuous linear isomorphisms preserving the original Euclidean differential calculus; normSq is the Euclidean square and dx is the original Lebesgue measure. ubar restricted to U is u and ubar is C∞ on U. All derivatives at positive times are independent of the arbitrary extension.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x,t>0,j,k as declared and put p=(x,t), w(y,r)=ubar(y,r)_k, T=(0,1), Xdir=(basis(j),0). F001 and continuous linear scalar projection give w C∞ on the open set U. Apply M006 over ℝ, with domain Space×ℝ, scalar codomain and both smoothness orders ∞: ∞+1=∞ supplies the order inequality, so Dw is C∞ on U. The derivative of the affine time injection r↦(x,r) sends h to (0,h); the derivative of y↦(y,t) sends h to (h,0). The ordinary chain rule identifies V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir, first as HasDerivAt or HasFDerivAt assertions, then as equalities by uniqueness. These identities hold on all U, not just at p. Evaluation at a fixed direction is continuous linear, so the identities and smoothness of Dw show that V and every Psp(j) are C∞ on U, componentwise and hence as finite vector-valued maps. In particular the actual time derivative of each coordinate of ubar is V. Record F002 with these first-derivative and smoothness facts.

produces.statement: V and Psp(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For every x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m, HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x0,r)_k0) V(x0,t1)_k0 t1; the spatial derivative in direction basis(j0) is Psp(j0,x0,t1)_k0. At the chosen p, V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir.

argument.text: Put Hess(v,w0)=D(Dw)(p)(v)(w0). Apply M006 again, this time to the C∞ map Dw with its continuous-linear-map codomain, and iterate for higher derivatives as needed; U is open and the ∞ order inequality remains valid. Differentiate the fixed evaluations from S002 by the chain rule. This gives ∂_t Psp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(T,Xdir), ∂_j V(x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,T), A(x,t)_k=Hess(T,T), and Ssp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,Xdir). F001 gives C² regularity of w at p because p∈U. Apply M005 over ℝ at order 2, where minSmoothness(ℝ,2)=2, to get Hess(T,Xdir)=Hess(Xdir,T). By the definition of W the common value is W(j,x,t)_k. The same derivative closure and fixed evaluations show A,Ssp(j),W(j) C∞ on U; this holds at every positive point and for every coordinate. Record F003: the full second-derivative regularity and the actual time derivative identities for V and Psp.

produces.statement: A, Ssp(j0), W(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For all x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m,j0∈Fin n, HasDerivAt (r↦V(x0,r)_k0) A(x0,t1)_k0 t1 and HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j0,x0,r)_k0) W(j0,x0,t1)_k0 t1. The spatial j0 derivative of V_k0 is W(j0)_k0 and the spatial j0 derivative of Psp(j0)_k0 is Ssp(j0)_k0.

argument.text: Apply M004 over ℝ to the time function V(x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using F003, to obtain derivative 2 V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k for its square. Apply M004 also to Psp(j,x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using its time derivative W(j,x,t)_k from F003, to obtain 2 Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k. The coordinate k and spatial index j are arbitrary; finite-sum differentiation therefore gives HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) [2∑_k V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k+2∑_j∑_k Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k] t. Finite distributivity identifies the bracket with d(x,t). Smooth finite products and sums of F002 and F003 also show e and d are C∞ on U. Record F004: the displayed HasDerivAt identity with derivative d, and C∞ regularity of e,d.

produces.statement: e and d are C∞ on U, and for the arbitrary x and t>0, HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t.

argument.text: The spatial derivative identities for ubar, Psp and V are their definitions; F002 and F003 verify that they are genuine derivatives at positive times. Combining F001–F004 proves all regularity, mixed-derivative and energy-derivative clauses. Since x,t,j,k were arbitrary, close their quantifiers. The identified Laplacian is exactly L=∑_j Ssp(j), and the identified density and measure give the original total energy expression E without any change of coefficient. This proves N001.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. The inequalities 0<t0/2<3t0/2 allow H006 to choose compact C such that u=q off C throughout J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2). All times of J are positive, so the definition of ubar gives the same equality for ubar. In particular t0∈I. Record F001: C is compact and ubar=q on Cᶜ×J.

argument.text: A compact subset C of the Hausdorff finite-dimensional space is closed. Thus O=Cᶜ×I is open. At each arbitrary p∈O the equality in F001 holds on a whole neighborhood: ubar is locally the constant q. Apply M007 to ubar and that constant on this neighborhood. The constant has zero derivative (its increments are zero), so D ubar(p)=0. This holds at every point of O. Reapply M007 to this derivative map and the zero map at every point of O; its derivative is again zero. Induction on the positive order now gives all iterated positive-order Fréchet derivatives zero on O: the first-order case is established; if the order-ℓ derivative map is zero throughout O, each point has a neighborhood on which that map is the constant zero, so M007 makes its next derivative zero there. The same chain-rule directional evaluations as in N001 identify V,A,Psp,Ssp,W with evaluations of the first two derivatives. Consequently V=A=Psp(j)=Ssp(j)=W(j)=0 on O for all j, and the formulas for e,d make both zero there. Record F002 with this universal vanishing conclusion.

produces.statement: Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on O=Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j1),Ssp(j1),W(j1),e,d vanish there for every j1∈Fin n.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r∈I and take the family of sections specified in the local declaration. By N001 each component section is continuous on the whole spatial space; e,d are continuous as well. Finite products, sums and dot products preserve continuity. F002 makes each of these sections zero off C. For an arbitrary section h in this family, support h⊆C. Since C is closed, its closure tsupport h is also contained in C; tsupport h is closed and hence a compact closed subset of the compact C. Apply M001 with domain Space, codomain ℝ and measure dx to h. This is a Borel real normed coordinate space; its Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. For example a compact set is contained in some finite coordinate box, whose product Lebesgue measure is finite, and monotonicity bounds the compact set's measure. Therefore the source gives dx-integrability of every such h. Record F003: all the stated sections at r have compact topological support contained in C and are integrable.

produces.statement: At the arbitrary r∈I, every h in family is continuous with tsupport h⊆C, has compact topological support, and is dx-integrable.

argument.text: The conclusions hold for every r∈I and every stated component, product, dot product and finite linear combination. Since t0∈I, this proves integrability of e(·,t0). The existence and vanishing conclusions depend only on the chosen slab and thus give the full existential statement N002 after closing the choice of C and the arbitrary t0. In particular every positive time has an integrable energy density. No vanishing assertion at the endpoints of J has been used.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and choose C from N002 with its full conclusions. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2), eta=t0/4>0, Ktime=[t0−eta,t0+eta], stime=(t0−eta,t0+eta). Explicitly t0−eta=3t0/4>t0/2 and t0+eta=5t0/4<3t0/2. Thus Ktime⊂I⊂(0,∞), and stime is an open neighborhood of t0. N002 supplies vanishing of d off C for all these times, and integrability and continuity of the spatial sections e,d throughout I.

Set Kprod=C×Ktime. Compactness of C from N002 and compactness of the closed bounded real interval Ktime show that Kprod is compact. It lies in U. N001 makes d continuous on U, so its restriction is continuous on Kprod. Apply M008 to d on Kprod to obtain a real bound for |d|. Record F001: there exists a real bound on Kprod. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. 𝓝 denotes the neighborhood filter. The support of a function is the set where its value is nonzero, tsupport is the closure of that set, and HasCompactSupport means this closure is compact. ContinuousOn means continuity relative to the indicated set. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function. Integrable means ae strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; IntegrableOn means integrability with respect to the restriction of the specified measure to the specified set. The Bochner integral uses the total library convention; for real integrable functions it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. A set indicator equals its function on that set and zero off it. An ae assertion holds outside a null set for the indicated measure. The extended norm on an ESeminormedAddMonoid is denoted by ‖·‖ₑ; real numbers have finite extended norm. Standard structure names retain their usual mathematical meanings: OpensMeasurableSpace says that open sets are measurable, BorelSpace identifies the measurable structure with the Borel structure, IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts says compact sets have finite measure, and IsAddHaarMeasure means an additive Haar measure. 479: /-- If a function is differentiable, and has two derivatives at `x`, then the second
480: derivative is symmetric. -/
481: theorem second_derivative_symmetric [IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜]
482:     {f' : E → E →L[𝕜] F} {f'' : E →L[𝕜] E →L[𝕜] F} {x : E}
483:     (hf : ∀ y, HasFDerivAt f (f' y) y) (hx : HasFDerivAt f' f'' x) (v w : E) : f'' v w = f'' w v :=
484:   second_derivative_symmetric_of_eventually (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hf) hx v w
485:

487: variable (𝕜) in
488: /-- `minSmoothness 𝕜 n` is the minimal smoothness exponent larger than or equal to `n` for which
489: one can do serious calculus in `𝕜`. If `𝕜` is `ℝ` or `ℂ`, this is just `n`. Otherwise,
490: this is `ω` as only analytic functions are well behaved on `ℚₚ`, say. -/
491: noncomputable irreducible_def minSmoothness (n : ℕ∞ω) :=
492:   if IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜 then n else ω
493: 
494: @[simp] lemma minSmoothness_of_isRCLikeNormedField [h : IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜] {n : ℕ∞ω} :
495:     minSmoothness 𝕜 n = n := by
496:   simp [minSmoothness, h]
497: 
498: lemma le_minSmoothness {n : ℕ∞ω} : n ≤ minSmoothness 𝕜 n := by
499:   simp only [minSmoothness]
500:   split_ifs <;> simp
501: 
502: lemma minSmoothness_add {n m : ℕ∞ω} : minSmoothness 𝕜 (n + m) = minSmoothness 𝕜 n + m := by
503:   simp only [minSmoothness]
504:   split_ifs <;> simp
505: 
506: lemma minSmoothness_monotone : Monotone (minSmoothness 𝕜) := by
507:   intro m n hmn
508:   simp only [minSmoothness]
509:   split_ifs <;> simp [hmn]
510: 
511: @[simp] lemma minSmoothness_eq_infty {n : ℕ∞ω} :
512:     minSmoothness 𝕜 n = ∞ ↔ (n = ∞ ∧ IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜) := by"}

7: [submission](submission-example.md), [source application](source-application-example.md)
8: and [quantified implication](quantified-implication-example.md) examples.
9: These examples show format and derivations, not certified benchmark answers.
10: 
11: The complete [guarded-definition example](guarded-definition-example.md) shows
12: how to organize a target that includes an object's existence and a property
13: of that object. For a real a let Q(r) mean r=a. R001 first proves N001, unique
14: existence of a Q witness, without using w. D002 then defines w as that unique
15: witness with requires=[N001]. R002 takes N001 as a direct input and proves the
16: full target: unique existence and w=a. Listing D002 in the global spec does
17: not let R001 use it before its guard. Do not hide an unproved guard in a
18: restricted domain when the frozen target requires a statement on the full
19: original domain. This pattern adds no new assumption or mathematical source.
20: 
21: ## Construct one coherent candidate
22: 
23: 1. For `target` and `definitions`, extract the original H, ambient parameters
24:    and global typed definitions. Preserve the original source locations. Do
25:    not change a parameter's mathematical kind while fixing its metadata.
26: 2. For `statement_closure`, design N/R interfaces from what their
27:    consumers actually need. Put the complete formulas, quantified conditions
28:    and space identifications into the exported statement, not only its body.
29: 3. For `dependency_closure` and `argument`, construct
30:    each proof unit alongside its premises. List exact source inputs or display
31:    a prior local derivation for every substantive fact beyond the fixed
32:    calculations. Split when local context changes; avoid a giant S whose
33:    changing objects must later be repaired one at a time.
34: 4. For `sources` and `applicability`, inspect each selected native/primary
35:    source, preserve its complete contract and ground each instantiated premise.
36:    A signature lookup or a sentence claiming a hypothesis is true is not proof
37:    of that hypothesis. Reuse an adequate proved source rather than re-proving
38:    it; a project-specific bridge still requires its displayed derivation.
39: 5. For object declarations and local scopes under dependency_closure, introduce objects and conditional premises
40:    at their actual first use. Keep witness bases and local F dependencies
41:    correct. Preserve exact coefficients and ranges when copying calculations.
42: 6. Run check_draft, correct its actual located records, inspect every own
43:    conditional packet, and report readiness below. The independent auditor
44:    applies the same criteria after definitive submission.
45: 
46: ## Canonical data shapes
47: 
48: Submit {spec,graph} using the schema, or preserve an own draft with
49: {base_candidate:N,patches:[...]}. The controller binds identity, input/pin
50: hashes, fixed language and exact native metadata; it does not rewrite proof
51: content. Use read_draft with a narrow pointer after an edit rejection.
52: Unique existing @ID/@symbol selectors work for own-stage reads/patches;
53: inserting array elements still uses numeric indices or /-. Audit evidence
54: uses standard JSON pointers instead of this selector extension.

57: start_line=1,end_line=20). It returns the actual numbered lines, total_lines
58: and complete text_sha256. Use an edit with exactly
59: {op:"replace_lines",path:"/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",start_line:4,end_line:5,
60: text:"replacement including its intended line endings",text_sha256:"the returned hash"}.
61: Ranges are positive and inclusive. Unselected text and line endings are
62: preserved; stale hashes are rejected. Include a line terminator when a
63: nonempty replacement precedes retained lines. Empty text deletes the range.
64: All ordinary validation and later Audit A still apply.
65: For reads only, an end beyond the string returns its remaining existing lines
66: and the actual range; the start must exist and at most 250 lines may be
67: requested. Line edits still reject any out-of-range end and never clamp it.
68: 
69: Each D has type, full definition, binders, used objects, D dependencies and
70: proved guards. Each H/E/M/N/P has full statement, definitions, binders, objects
71: and appropriate source/origin fields. Each R has direct inputs, one output,
72: definitions, rules, locals, argument and real source applications. Each S has
73: actual text, uses, earlier uses_local, objects, complete produces F statements,
74: and assumption introductions/discharges. Each source application has input,
75: at:Sddd, bindings and actual hypothesis_checks. See the linked schema/examples
76: for exact names. source_uses can serialize one already selected M/E into the
77: R.inputs, S.uses and application together; supply the actual mathematical
78: bindings and grounds yourself.

81: D.definition may be {from_task:"input ID",start_line:N,end_line:M}, just like
